title: Sleep the way you were meant to
passage: Mossgrove Calm drops blend valerian, chamomile and lemon balm, with nothing cooked up in a lab. Your body knows the difference. Why fill your system with synthetic sleep aids when the earth already grows something better? 30 nights for $24, or your money back.
cue: Why fill your system with synthetic sleep aids when the earth already grows something better?
explanation: Mossgrove claims its drops beat sleep medications simply because they come from plants. Being plant-based says nothing about whether they work or are safer; that takes evidence.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_tradition: The ad never says the herbs are an old remedy; its pitch is that plants beat anything made in a lab.

passage:
Kemi: Heads up, the cleaning crew is starting to use a hospital-grade disinfectant in the hallways and laundry room.
Bjorn: Ugh. I'm asking them to switch to plain vinegar. Something that starts out as apples isn't going to hurt anyone, and it'll handle germs as well as anything mixed in a factory.
Kemi: Is that true about the germs, though?
cue: Something that starts out as apples isn't going to hurt anyone
explanation: Bjorn assumes vinegar is harmless and just as effective because it comes from fruit instead of a factory. Whether a cleaner is safe or kills germs depends on testing, not on what it's made from.

whyNot.fal_is_ought: Bjorn isn't jumping from how things are to how they ought to be; he assumes that coming from fruit, not a factory, makes a cleaner safe and effective.

title: Pricey, but the clean caffeine is worth it
passage: Tastes like fresh grapefruit, and the can design is gorgeous. The caffeine comes from green coffee beans instead of the synthetic stuff in regular energy drinks, so it's much gentler on your heart. I'm comfortable drinking three a day now. Only complaint: at $3.50 a can, it adds up fast.
cue: instead of the synthetic stuff in regular energy drinks, so it's much gentler on your heart
explanation: Priscilla assumes caffeine from beans is easier on the heart than synthetic caffeine. It's the same molecule either way, so three cans a day carries the same caffeine load.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_tradition: Nothing here rests on custom or history; the flaw is treating 'from beans' as automatically gentler.

passage: Switched from cushioned trainers to barefoot shoes in January. My calves screamed for a month, so ease in if you try it. But our feet evolved to run on bare ground, so all that foam is just a crutch that weakens them. No more padding for me, ever. Ten-miler this weekend!
cue: our feet evolved to run on bare ground, so all that foam is just a crutch
explanation: Marco gives sensible advice about easing in, then argues cushioning is harmful because barefoot running is how feet evolved. What feet did naturally doesn't settle what's best for a modern runner.

whyNot.fal_is_ought: It's not a general leap from facts to duties; Marco treats the natural state of feet as automatically the healthy one.

source: Parent rep Sunita Varma · Brookside school board
passage: The proposal before us replaces the artificially sweetened yogurt in our cafeterias with versions sweetened with honey and fruit concentrate, and I think that's the right call. Whatever the lab reports say about the sweetener, children's bodies are built for real food, not compounds engineered in a factory. Real ingredients are always the healthier choice.
cue: children's bodies are built for real food, not compounds engineered in a factory
explanation: Sunita sets aside the lab reports on the sweetener and prefers honey and fruit concentrate because they're 'real food'. Both are still added sugar, so naturalness alone doesn't settle which is healthier.

whyNot.fal_is_ought: Sunita isn't moving from facts to moral duties; she assumes natural ingredients are healthier simply because they're natural.

title: Community garden votes to allow only plant-derived pesticides
passage: Members of the Larkmoor community garden voted 23-9 to ban synthetic pesticides from the plots this spring. Member Imogen Tate, who proposed the change, said sprays 'derived from plants work with the garden's ecosystem instead of against it.' The new rule allows pyrethrin and neem-based products, which members say they will apply more often to compensate.
cue: derived from plants work with the garden's ecosystem instead of against it
explanation: Imogen argues plant-derived sprays are better for the garden because of where they come from. Pyrethrins are toxic to bees and fish too; effects, not origins, decide ecological harm.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_tradition: Imogen's case isn't that plant sprays are traditional; it's that coming from plants makes them ecologically gentler.

title: Finally, no more stinging eyes
passage: Switched my daughter to a mineral sunscreen this summer. Zinc oxide blocks both UVA and UVB, and our pediatrician pointed out that mineral formulas are less likely to irritate sensitive skin and sting eyes, which was exactly our problem with the old one. Two months in, no more tears at the pool. For her, this is the better pick.
cue: mineral formulas are less likely to irritate sensitive skin and sting eyes
explanation: Rania picks the mineral sunscreen for specific reasons: broad UV protection and less irritation, which matched her daughter's problem. The choice rests on effects, not on 'mineral' sounding natural.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_nature: Rania never claims mineral means better in general; she chooses it for specific, supported effects that fit her daughter's skin.

source: City engineer Mehmet Aydin · Fenmoor flood forum
passage: Restoring the 40-acre marsh along Fen Creek sounds like a feel-good idea, so here are the numbers. Our model shows it would hold about 30 million gallons in a 100-year storm, roughly what the proposed concrete basin holds, at a third of the cost and with lower upkeep. On capacity and cost, restoration is simply the better flood plan for Fenmoor.
cue: Our model shows it would hold about 30 million gallons in a 100-year storm
explanation: Mehmet prefers the marsh, but not because it's natural: he compares storage capacity, cost and upkeep with the concrete option. The evidence carries the conclusion.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_nature: Mehmet's case rests on modeled capacity and cost, not on the marsh being natural; if the numbers flipped, so would his conclusion.
